title: Commercial Fusion Energy in 2026: Two-Thirds Built, Funding on the Line

stats.label: ITER tokamak core installed
stats.detail: Six of nine sector modules lowered into the pit, almost six months ahead of schedule; the last is targeted for mid-2027.

stats.label: Cumulative private fusion funding
stats.detail: Reported since 2021; a record $4.48B was raised worldwide in the 12 months to July 2026.

stats.label: U.S. fusion companies
stats.detail: Most are pursuing tokamaks or stellarators; others use laser-based inertial confinement.

stats.label: U.S. target for fusion deployment
stats.detail: DOE Fusion Science and Technology Roadmap issued June 2026; the Office of Fusion was created in November 2025.

stats.label: FY2027 fusion energy sciences funding
stats.detail: Below the $805.7M enacted, though 2022 legislation authorized up to $1.1B.

quotes.text: The plan isn't the problem. We all agree on the plan. The X factor is the funding. If we underfund the U.S. fusion program and we cut vital scope, we can all watch the timeline to commercialisation slip.
quotes.source: Robb Hughes, Realta Fusion, in Reuters

quotes.text: Private developers have not yet achieved "net energy gain," the point where a fusion reaction produces more energy than was used to start and sustain it.
quotes.source: Reuters, US roadmap targets fusion deployment by mid 2030s

quotes.text: With six modules now in place, we are demonstrating that this technical approach is delivering tangible results on the project's critical path.
quotes.source: Pietro Barabaschi, ITER Director-General, ITER Organization

quotes.text: ITER is primarily an exploratory science initiative and is not designed or intended to produce electricity.
quotes.source: CRS Report R48866, Toward Commercial Fusion Energy

takeaway: Fusion's remaining race is engineering and funding, not physics: the machine assembly is ahead of schedule while the U.S. program is funded below its authorized level.
